title: Open Neuromorphic Strategic Roadmap Announcement: ONR 2.0, Z2S Curriculum, Taxonomy & Benchmarking Consultation
summary: On 2026-08-29, Open Neuromorphic announced a strategic roadmap addressing community needs for vendor-neutral benchmarking and education. The initiative includes relaunching the Open Neuromorphic Research (ONR) program with an open 'Process as Provenance' model to ensure reproducibility via Zenodo DOIs. A new cloud-native 'Zero to Silicon' curriculum guides learners from biophysical models to Verilog RTL synthesis within Google Colab, eliminating local toolchain requirements. Additionally, a Master Taxonomy Initiative organizes hardware and software knowledge by technical expertise, application domains, and availability status. Finally, Open Neuromorphic seeks community input on its role in standardized benchmarking, offering three paths: hosting open leaderboards, aggregating existing evaluation suites, or creating a dedicated peer-reviewed track for reproducibility audits.
tldr: Open Neuromorphic unveiled a 2026 roadmap featuring ONR 2.0 for reproducible research, a cloud-native 'Zero to Silicon' education curriculum, and new taxonomy/benchmarking initiatives.
evidence: Today, we are excited to unveil our strategic roadmap across four foundational pillars designed to scale our community infrastructure and accelerate neuromorphic development.
ONR 2.0 introduces a 'Process as Provenance' model... culminating in citable Zenodo DOIs.

- 100% Cloud-Native: The entire pipeline—from Python reference models to inline Verilog RTL synthesis and verilator compilation—runs directly inside Google Colab with zero local installations required.
Our Core Guarantees: Neutrality & Open Science Regardless of which direction the community chooses, ONM's stance is firm: - Strict Vendor Neutrality
- 100% Open & Locably Reproducible: All benchmark harnesses... must be open source (MIT/Apache 2.0/CC-BY) and verifiable on local developer hardware without black-box dependencies.
